question: 7 years ago, the age of a father was 20 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the present ages be F (Father) and S (Son).

Given 7 years ago: (F − 7) = 2 × (S − 7) + 20 ⇒ F − 2S = 13

Assume after y years, the Father will be twice the Son's age: (F + y) = 2 × (S + y)

Simplifying the future condition gives: F − 2S = y

Since we already established that F − 2S = 13, the required time y must be 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ 7 years ago, the Father's age was 20 more than twice the Son's age.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Future Age = Present Age + Number of Years
